name: tear-ticket

frames.best_why: The stub is hinged away with a visible torn gap along the perforation, showing the tear itself.

tagline: Event ticket tilts in 3D; grab the perforated stub and tear it free.
summary: A boarding-pass style ticket with a photo header, trip details and a perforated stub. Moving the mouse tips it in perspective; dragging the stub pulls thin fibres until it rips away and tumbles off.
appearance: A wide rounded ticket in dark grey, a mountain photo across the top under the route line, three labelled details beneath and a dotted perforation separating a narrow stub that shows the seat.
behaviour: The card leans toward the pointer in a soft 3D tilt, with the photo and text shifting at slightly different depths. Dragging the stub pulls thin fibres across the perforation until they snap and the stub falls away.
demo_content: Alpine Express day pass from Zermatt to Gornergrat, seat 14C, gate B7, passenger Maya Chen.
search_phrases: event ticket with tear off stub
use_when: A ticket, voucher or pass benefits from a tactile reveal that marks it used, not just a checkbox.
avoid_when: Dragging is pointer-only, the tear needs motion to land, and it suits one-off tickets rather than long lists.
customise: Width, height, stub size, image, body children, stub slot, background, border, tilt strength and tear feel are props; the tear simulation is fixed.
weight_why: Springs follow the pointer and a hand-written loop runs only while tearing.

a11y.note: The stub is a labelled button and Enter tears it, but there is no visible focus ring on it.

polish_why: Convincing paper ticket with a real tear; text over the photo is partly lost in the lighter sky.
title: Tear Ticket
